items.title: IGNIS unified chip tray — history + contextual
items.why: IGNIS has two independent memory surfaces — PAGE_QUERIES contextual chips (S210) and vs_ignis_history 10-query log (S199) — that never appear together. A returning visitor's first open of the oracle shows only generic page chips, ignoring that they queried 'VoidFall release' last session. Merging them into one chip tray (Recent | Topics tabs, or a blended row) collapses re-engagement friction to zero and makes IGNIS feel like it knows the visitor.
items.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js mount(): read vs_ignis_history from localStorage (first 3 entries, within 72h); if entries exist, prepend a 'Recent' chip row above PAGE_QUERIES chips; each chip is one-tap → auto-run that query. Label rows with 'Recent' and 'Topics'. Use existing chip CSS. No new deps.

L1.recipe: Add 2 history chips below contextual chips (no tabs, no labels) — minimal change, immediate value for returning users.

L2.recipe: Tabbed tray 'Recent ▸ Topics' — history chips first tab, PAGE_QUERIES second tab; tab state in sessionStorage. Defaults to 'Recent' when history exists, else 'Topics'.

L3.recipe: Blended smart row: score each history query by recency × relevance to current page path; sort + interleave with top 2 page chips; show top 5 total. No tabs needed — the blend surfaces what matters most.

items.title: Game discovery quiz — 'What should I play?'
items.why: The /games/ page shows all games in a grid but has no funnel for a first-time visitor who doesn't know which to start with. A 3-question quiz (genre taste, session length, mood) that recommends a specific game with a direct play link converts browsers into players. Zero new deps — the game catalog data is already in public-intelligence.json. This is the missing first-mile onboarding for new visitors.
items.recipe: Create assets/game-discovery-quiz.js: renders a 3-step quiz panel (genre: action/strategy/story; session: quick/medium/deep; mood: casual/competitive/immersive). Maps answer combination → game recommendation using a static mapping keyed on public-intelligence.json 'tags'. Add to /games/index.html as a dismissible panel above the grid. predicate-load via ambient-loader.

L1.recipe: Static mapping only — 8 combinations → 2 games each. Single question (genre only) to reduce scope. CTA links directly to game page.

L2.recipe: 3-question quiz with full 27-combination mapping; shows game cover + tagline + play CTA; result written to vs_game_rec localStorage for ambient-loader to pick up on /games/.

L3.recipe: Quiz + IGNIS integration: after recommendation, offer 'Ask IGNIS about [game]' with the chip pre-filled; track quiz:started/completed/recommendation_shown/play_clicked in RUM.

items.title: Web-push feature — Worker endpoint + client subscribe UI
items.why: VAPID keys are READY in the secrets gateway (cloudflare.vapid, 3/3 keys present) and the push-prompt.js stub exists. The only missing pieces are the Worker endpoint that stores subscriptions and the subscribe.js client that calls it. This is the highest-priority carry from S210 — a direct engagement-retention driver that lets the studio reach members on new ship days without email or social.
items.recipe: 1. Package-trust check web-push@9.1.0. 2. Add Worker route /v/push-subscribe (POST: store subscription JSON in KV under vs:push:sub:<hashed-endpoint>; GET: check subscription exists). 3. Create assets/push-subscribe.js: on /vault-member/, renders a subscribe/unsubscribe toggle; calls /v/push-subscribe on click; uses navigator.serviceWorker + PushManager.subscribe with VAPID public key. 4. Register a minimal sw.js Service Worker that handles push events. 5. Run push-dispatch.mjs --test to confirm end-to-end.

L1.recipe: Worker /v/push-subscribe endpoint only (no client UI). Stores subscription, returns 200/409. Manually test with push-dispatch.mjs using a hard-coded endpoint.

L2.recipe: Full feature: Worker endpoint + sw.js push handler + assets/push-subscribe.js client UI on /vault-member/. End-to-end test via push-dispatch.mjs --test.

L3.recipe: L2 + SW caches IGNIS search index on activate for instant offline IGNIS; push notification bodies are personalized per member's last 2 IGNIS queries (stored in KV alongside subscription).

items.title: IGNIS answer-derived follow-up questions
items.why: After IGNIS delivers an answer, the user is left with raw text and no next step. Extracting 3 follow-up questions from the answer — derived from entities and concepts mentioned — would keep them in a discovery loop and dramatically increase oracle session depth. These are NOT generic 'related topics' chips (S210) but answer-specific: if the answer mentions 'VoidFall combat system', the follow-up is 'Tell me more about VoidFall combat'. This turns single-question lookups into multi-turn discovery sessions.
items.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js, after answer renders: parse result.text for entity mentions using the existing search index token set. Extract top 3 unique entities not in the original query. Render as 'Dig deeper:' chips below the answer. Click triggers a new query with 'Tell me more about [entity]' pre-filled. Add oracle:followup_shown + oracle:followup_click RUM events.

L1.recipe: Show 2 static follow-up suggestions per page type (e.g. on /games/ always offer 'What are the game mechanics?' after any answer). Quick but generic.

L2.recipe: Entity extraction from answer text using index token set; 3 follow-up chips below answer; oracle:followup_shown + oracle:followup_click RUM.

L3.recipe: L2 + confidence scoring: entity chips ranked by frequency in answer × rarity in index (TF-IDF proxy). Shows the most unique/interesting follow-up first, not just the most frequent.

items.title: IGNIS results semantic clustering by theme
items.why: IGNIS currently returns a ranked flat list of matches. For multi-document queries ('tell me about VaultSpark'), the result is a wall of text blending gameplay, lore, tech, and community mentions. Grouping the source documents by theme cluster (Gameplay · Story · Technical · Community) before assembling the answer gives structure to long responses and lets the visitor scan to the dimension they care about.
items.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js answer(): after computing scored matches, classify each source document into one of 4 clusters using keyword sets from the index (gameplay: 'combat', 'level', 'score'; story: 'narrative', 'lore', 'world'; technical: 'performance', 'engine', 'build'; community: 'member', 'vault', 'rank'). Render cluster headers in the output. Only applies when ≥3 sources; falls back to flat list for focused queries.

L1.recipe: 2 buckets only (Gameplay / Studio) — minimal keyword classifier, one divider line between sections.

L2.recipe: 4-cluster system (Gameplay · Story · Technical · Community) with labeled section headers in the answer output.

L3.recipe: L2 + cluster confidence threshold: only render a cluster header when ≥2 sources qualify; mixed sources go into 'General'. Add oracle:cluster_shown RUM per cluster.

items.title: Changelog page — inline push subscribe CTA
items.why: The returning-visitor strip (S210) links to /changelog/ and is the most focused 'new ships' surface on the site. A visitor who clicked that strip is already in a 'show me what's new' mindset — the ideal moment to offer push notifications. A single subscribe banner at the top of /changelog/ (dismissible, only shown once per session) converts that intent into a durable channel. Depends on web-push-complete (item #3) being shipped first.
items.recipe: In /changelog/index.html, after web-push is live: add a one-line banner 'Get push notifications when something ships →' with a Subscribe button that calls push-subscribe.js API. Dismiss writes vs_cl_push_prompt=1. Predicate: push supported AND not already subscribed AND not dismissed. Add push:changelog_prompt_shown + push:subscribed RUM.

L1.recipe: Static HTML banner with inline onclick that calls window.VaultPush.subscribe() — no new asset, just markup addition to changelog page.

L2.recipe: L1 + animated slide-in (CSS only); shows 'You're subscribed!' confirmation in-place on success; adds RUM events.

L3.recipe: L2 + shows the last push notification sent (from KV metadata) as social proof: 'Last notification: VoidFall beta dropped 3 days ago'.

items.title: Vault Member portal — rank progression + milestone display
items.why: The vault-member portal exists but doesn't show what matters most to a member: where they are in the 9-tier rank system and what they need to reach the next tier. This is the core retention mechanic of the membership — make rank progress visible and the next milestone concrete. Currently a member can only infer their rank from their account metadata. Deepening this surface turns it from a receipt page into a progression dashboard.
items.recipe: In /projects/vault-member/index.html: after auth state resolves (identity.js), read member.rank + member.points from Supabase member_profile table. Render: current rank badge + name, points bar toward next tier threshold (from data/rank-thresholds.json), next unlock label. Graceful fallback for zero-point accounts. Add portal:rank_shown RUM.

L1.recipe: Show current rank badge (static SVG/emoji per tier) + tier name. No progress bar — just rank identity.

L2.recipe: Full rank + points bar + next milestone label. Reads from Supabase member_profile.

L3.recipe: L2 + recent activity log (last 5 rank events from member_activity table) + achievement unlock notifications (in-page toast). Sets up the visual foundation for web-push achievement alerts.
